# DDA Optimizations (Rejected/Retained)

Also called: Boundary event counts, DDA region traversal, Explicit zero-event guards, Per-ray subtree caching, Redundant floor removal

## Overview
This family article catalogs algorithmic modifications to Digital Differential Analyzer (DDA) ray traversal, evaluating their CPU and GPU performance impact to determine which optimizations are retained in the final implementation [S1, unofficial]. It distinguishes between successful optimizations that reduce computational overhead and rejected variants where added complexity or overhead outweighs benefits [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The optimizations operate under the parent family's constraints: branch unification, memory coalescing, occupancy management, and implicit clipping [G]. All retained optimizations preserve exact geometric correctness of surface intersections and image byte accumulation [S1, unofficial]. Rejected optimizations occur when reduced traversal steps (e.g., fewer tree visits or skipped empty regions) are offset by increased per-step overhead, such as complex ownership checks, repeated CPU costs, or negative GPU warp efficiency impacts [S1, unofficial]. Evaluation compares cumulative CPU costs, actual work counters, and complete-frame measurements across CPU and GPU workloads using specific benchmark configurations (CPU1, CPU6, CPU12, GPU fork-seven) [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### DDA Region Traversal
This optimization compares upstream world representations to optimize how the DDA crosses compressed uniform regions [S1, unofficial]. It is documented in the region DDA profile, which records cumulative CPU costs, actual work counters, and one rejected search optimization [S1, unofficial]. What sets it apart is its focus on hierarchical region crossing rather than per-voxel stepping. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

### Corrected Event Counting
This optimization replaces the baseline binary search for event detection with a bounded estimate followed by an exact plane correction [S1, unofficial]. It provides repeated gains on CPU12 and separate GPU measurements [S1, unofficial]. It is distinguished by its hybrid estimation-and-correction approach. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

### Per-Ray Subtree Caching
This optimization caches subtree information on a per-ray basis to reduce tree visits during traversal [S1, unofficial]. It was rejected because fewer tree visits did not offset the added ownership work, and the retained DDA remains unchanged [S1, unofficial]. It is distinguished by its per-ray state management. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

### Explicit Zero-Event Guards
This optimization checks for short-circuiting conditions where no events are expected, allowing the traversal to skip calculations [S1, unofficial]. Four short-circuiting prototypes were tested [S1, unofficial]. Broader guards regress on GPU, while the smallest avoids advancement plane calculations but adds a repeated CPU cost, leaving the retained DDA unchanged [S1, unofficial]. It is distinguished by its conditional early-exit logic. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

### Redundant Floor Removal
This optimization simplifies the retained event estimate by removing redundant floor operations [S1, unofficial]. It preserves exact surfaces and image bytes [S1, unofficial]. GPU fork-seven measurements improve in two batches, while parallel CPU samples favor the baseline [S1, unofficial]. It is distinguished by its arithmetic simplification of the event estimate. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

### Boundary Event Counts
This optimization reuses the known integer limit for axes leaving a region to optimize boundary event detection [S1, unofficial]. It preserves exact surfaces and image bytes [S1, unofficial]. CPU1, CPU6, and CPU12 improve in repeated complete-window measurements, while GPU gains remain inconclusive [S1, unofficial]. It is distinguished by its reuse of fixed integer bounds for region exits. When to choose it and its link: Not given in the sources.

## Background
The optimizations are derived from the development and profiling of the Bend voxel renderer's DDA traversal component [S1, unofficial]. The work is documented in internal reports within the `aivv73/bend-voxel` repository, specifically `docs/dda-optimization.md`, `docs/dda-profile.md`, `docs/dda-estimate.md`, `docs/dda-cursor.md`, `docs/dda-zero.md`, `docs/dda-floor.md`, and `docs/dda-boundary.md` [S1, unofficial].
